rules.name: Questionnaire flow overview
rules.statement: The questionnaire has exactly eight steps in this order. Each question is asked once and its answer is reused for every receiving party; a question is only asked when at least one party needs the answer for this person. Answers are saved as the employee goes and they can resume until they submit; submitting needs one confirmation on a summary page.

table.then: Always: first name, last name, date of birth, first working day
Always: street, house number (or 'no house number'), postcode, town and country as on the first working day; canton only if the country is Switzerland
Only employees living in Switzerland: nationality; C permit (yes/no) only if not Swiss

Civil status from everyone; spouse's date of birth if married, registered partnership or separated; spouse's nationality, C permit and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland only for non-Swiss employees without C permit living in Switzerland who are married or in a registered partnership
Only employees living in Liechtenstein or Germany (always subject to source tax): daily return and non-return days; certificate of residence for Germany
Only employees subject to source tax, except Liechtenstein residents in principle not liable: denomination, spouse gainfully employed (married or registered partnership), has children
Only if source tax details are asked and the employee has children: one block per child, no maximum
Always: summary and one confirmation; permit reminder for non-Swiss employees and employees living abroad

rules.name: Insurance start date
rules.statement: The pension fund insurance start date is derived from the first working day only: if the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise on the 1st of the following month. It is always derived again from the latest first working day.

rules.name: Civil status for the pension fund
rules.statement: The fund only accepts Single, Married, Divorced and Widowed. Registered partnership and Separated are entered as Married (with the spouse's/partner's date of birth); the other values are entered as they are (assumption D-003).

rules.name: Canton for the pension fund
rules.statement: Employees living in Switzerland: the canton they chose. Employees living abroad: the canton of the place of work, Zurich for Muster AG, not asked (assumption D-002).

rules.name: Subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee living abroad is subject to source tax whatever their nationality. An employee living in Switzerland is subject only if not Swiss, without a C permit, and not married to (or in a registered partnership with) a Swiss national or C-permit holder who lives in Switzerland. Separated counts as single. 'Here' in HR's wording means Switzerland (assumption D-043).
inputs: Spouse Swiss or holds a C permit
rules.expression: (is_set(address_country) and address_country != "Switzerland") or (address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and is_set(civil_status) and not (civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and spouse_residence_country == "yes" and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_holds_c_permit == "yes")))

rules.name: Liechtenstein resident in principle not liable
rules.statement: An employee living in Liechtenstein who returns daily, or who does not return daily but expects at most 45 non-return days, is in principle not liable to source tax, subject to the double taxation agreement. Lonio shows this instead of a tariff code, flags it for HR and skips the remaining tariff questions.

table.then: in principle no source tax liability (flagged for HR)
in principle no source tax liability (flagged for HR)

rules.name: Double taxation agreement note (Liechtenstein)
rules.statement: For an employee living in Liechtenstein without daily return and with more than 45 non-return days, the plain tariff code is recorded and the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement' is recorded separately next to it and flagged for HR; the note is not part of the code.

table.then: note recorded and flagged for HR
no separate note (in principle not liable)
no separate note (in principle not liable)

rules.name: Civil status group for source tax
rules.statement: For source tax, Married and Registered partnership count as 'married or registered partnership'; Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated count as 'single, divorced, separated or widowed', as in the calculator.
rules.expression: if_else(civil_status == null, null, if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "Married or registered partnership", "Single, divorced, separated or widowed"))

rules.name: Residence for the tariff calculation
rules.statement: The calculator's residence answers are derived from the home address country instead of being asked again: Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein or another country. Switzerland and other countries give the base tariff without further residence questions.
rules.expression: if_else(address_country == "Switzerland", "Switzerland", if_else(address_country == "Germany", "Germany", if_else(address_country == "Liechtenstein", "Liechtenstein", if_else(address_country == null, null, "Other country"))))

rules.name: Church-tax suffix
rules.statement: Roman Catholic, Christ Catholic or Evangelical Reformed gives the suffix Y; none or other gives N.

when: Roman Catholic, Christ Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

rules.expression: if_else(confession == "Roman Catholic, Christ Catholic or Evangelical Reformed", "Y", if_else(confession == "None or other", "N", null))

rules.name: Per-child result
rules.statement: Each child block yields one result: counted, counted with H (single, divorced, separated or widowed employees only) or not counted. Observed calculator results win over the general rule (D-046); rows marked inferred are checked against the calculator before go-live (D-009).
rules.expression: if_else(child_age_status == null, null, if_else(child_age_status == "Neither", "not counted", if_else(child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_custody == "Sole custody", if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", "counted", "counted with H"), if_else(child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_custody == "Shared custody" and child_common_household_other_parent == "yes", if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", "counted", child_common_household_other_parent == "no" and child_alternating_custody == "yes", if_else(child_main_financial_contributor == "Myself", if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", "counted", "counted with H"), "not counted"), if_else(child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_custody == "Shared custody" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no" and child_alternating_custody == "no", if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", "not counted", "counted with H"), if_else(child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no" and (child_shared_custody == "yes" or child_parental_care == "yes") and child_alternating_custody == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "Myself", if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", "counted", "counted with H"), if_else(child_age_status == "Adult in first education" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "yes", if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", "counted", if_else(child_main_financial_contributor == "Myself", "counted with H", "not counted")), if_else(child_age_status == "Adult in first education" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no" and child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes", if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", "counted", "counted with H"), if_else(child_age_status == "Adult in first education" and child_same_household == "no" and child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes", "counted", "not counted"))))))))))

rules.name: Number of counted children (child digit)
rules.statement: The child digit of the tariff code is the number of children whose result is 'counted' or 'counted with H', summed over all child blocks. Without children it is 0. (The internal expression evaluates one child block; it is summed over all blocks.)
rules.expression: if_else(has_children == "yes" and child_result in ["counted", "counted with H"], 1, 0)

rules.name: Base tariff letter
rules.statement: Married or registered partnership: C if the spouse/partner is gainfully employed (or receives replacement income), otherwise B. Single, divorced, separated or widowed: H if any child is counted with H, otherwise A. Earned income is always assumed, so G does not occur (D-006).
rules.expression: if_else(not (subject_to_source_tax and (address_country != "Liechtenstein" or non_return_days_45 == "yes")), null, if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", if_else(spouse_gainful_employment == "yes", "C", if_else(spouse_gainful_employment == "no", "B", null)), if_else(calculator_civil_status == null, null, if_else(has_children == "yes" and child_result == "counted with H", "H", "A"))))

rules.name: Cross-border (Grenzgänger) tariff applies
rules.statement: For an employee living in Germany the cross-border tariff applies if they return daily and have a certificate of residence ('not yet' counts as no), or if they do not return daily, daily return would be reasonable and they do not expect more than 60 non-return days. Otherwise the normal tariff applies.

rules.name: Tariff letter
rules.statement: When the cross-border tariff applies, the base letter is replaced: A by L, B by M, C by N, H by P (and G by Q, which cannot occur for onboarding). Otherwise the base letter is used.

rules.name: Permit reminder
rules.statement: At the end of the questionnaire, every non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland and every employee living abroad (whatever their nationality, which is not asked) is reminded to bring their permit on the first working day. HR provides the wording before go-live, so that a Swiss citizen living abroad can see it does not apply to them. It collects no data.

rules.name: Discard answers that no longer apply
rules.statement: Answers to questions that no longer apply after an earlier answer changes are kept while the employee goes back and forth, and discarded on submission. The same applies after an HR change.

when: on submission or after an HR change
table.then: answers to questions that no longer apply are discarded

rules.name: Read-only after submission
rules.statement: After submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee and never reopened. Later changes (move, marriage, new child, late certificate of residence, corrected nationality, first working day) are made by HR; every derived result is derived again from the latest answers, and results depending on questions never asked show 'incomplete - HR must complete' until HR enters the answers.

table.then: read-only for the employee; changes by HR only

open_questions.question: Does Lonio's computed tariff code match the Zurich calculator for the unexplored paths: the residence block for tariffs A/B/H, the inferred per-child rows, more than 3 children, and the H3N/P3N examples?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lonio now owns the tariff result instead of HR clicking through the calculator; unverified paths could produce wrong source tax codes.
options: Domain expert compares computed codes with the calculator for the listed paths before go-live
Go live and fall back to HR's manual check for unexplored paths
open_questions.recommendation: Domain expert check before go-live (D-009); observed rows win over derived ones (D-046).
